D013-D008_h002.question:

I’ll be out in the shed, checking tools, and suddenly my eyes well up for no clear reason. Sometimes I hide it from her, sometimes I can’t.

On rainy days I just drift in and out of sleep in the chair. It’s like my head is full of cotton; I’ll stand in the field trying to remember what I came out there to do. Doing the books or deciding when to plant just feels confusing and slow.

More and more, I catch myself thinking it might be easier if I just didn’t wake up one morning. I’m not making any plans to hurt myself, but the idea of just being done with everything doesn’t scare me.

There are odd stretches where I suddenly feel like I’ve got more energy than usual and sleep less, getting a lot done around the farm for a few days, but they don’t last, and then I’m back to this heavy, foggy place. It’s made keeping up with the farm and family a lot harder.

D013-D008_h023.question:
It’s like I’ve been hollowed out for the last year or so—maybe a bit more than a year. I still go to showings, but I feel like I’m just walking my body through the motions. With clients I can fake being upbeat, but as soon as I’m alone it’s just…nothing. Not sad exactly, more like there’s no color to anything.

Sleep has gotten weird. I fall asleep okay, but I keep waking up at 2 or 3 a.m. and then I’m just staring at the ceiling for hours, mind racing about listings, bills, my ex, my kids. By the time the alarm goes off, I feel exhausted.

I’m also noticing my mind doesn’t feel as sharp. I lose my car keys constantly, forget where I parked at a showing, or blank on clients’ names even when I just met them. It’s embarrassing in my line of work.

There are moments, usually when I’m crossing a busy street or standing on a balcony in a high-rise, where I get this sudden urge—like, “What if I just stepped off?” It’s quick and intense, not something I’ve planned, but it scares me. All of this has made it a lot harder to keep my business going the way it used to.

D013-D008_h024.question:
It’s hard to explain… For the last year, maybe a bit more, it’s like someone turned the volume down on everything. I don’t really feel much of anything anymore—good or bad. My wife says I seem distant; I just feel flat. I go to the plant, I walk the line, I sign off the reports, but it’s like I’m doing it on autopilot. I make more mistakes now, or stare at a defect and can’t decide if it’s really a problem—my head just feels foggy, like I’m thinking through cotton.

Sleep’s messed up. I’m up at three or four most mornings, wide awake, and then I just lie there, going over numbers, people’s faces, stupid interactions from years ago. I can’t get back to sleep, so by the time I start work I’m already wiped.

Every now and then, out of nowhere, I’ll be driving over an overpass and this thought flashes in—“What if I just turned the wheel and went off?” Or I’m crossing the street and picture stepping out in front of a truck. It jolts me; I don’t have an actual plan, but the urge scares me.

There are times, though, when I’ll get these odd bursts of energy—clean the garage at midnight, start sketching ideas to overhaul the whole inspection process, talking too fast to my team. My wife says I seem “wired” on those days. They don’t last long, and then I crash back into this dull, heavy feeling again. It’s starting to affect my work and my marriage; I’m not the guy I used to be.

D013-D008_h025.question:
It’s hard to describe… for the last year or so, maybe a bit longer, I just feel hollow most of the time. It’s like I’m going through the motions with the kids and the house, but inside there’s nothing—no real sadness, no joy, just… blank. I sleep enough hours, sometimes more than I should, but I wake up feeling like I never slept at all, like I’ve run a marathon in my sleep.

I used to be able to follow a book or a TV show while folding laundry; now I’ll read the same page three times and still not remember it. Even keeping up with a simple conversation with my husband, my mind drifts off and I lose track of what we were talking about.

Every once in a while—maybe a couple of times a month—I’ll get these sudden, almost intrusive urges, like a flash in my head telling me to just step in front of a car or jump off the overpass when I’m driving. It’s not like I’ve made a plan or really want to die, but the thoughts feel sharp and scary when they happen.

There are also these odd spells where, for a few days, I feel unusually wired and talkative, staying up late with a burst of energy to reorganize the closets or start big projects, but they never last long, and then I crash back into that empty, tired state again. All of this has made it much harder to keep up with the kids and basic chores; things pile up, and I feel overwhelmed by even small tasks.
